tasks.short: Confirm guest reservations after the guest asks.

steps.what: Hear the guest request for reservations.
Check free rooms before the clerk will confirm.
Confirm reservations only after the guest asked.
Review the reservation record before it is stored.
Write confirmed reservations the clerk accepted.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk hears the request, checks free rooms on {OPS_SYSTEM}, and confirms with the guest. The clerk then checks the filled reservation. {OPS_SYSTEM} stores that accepted record and does not confirm a stay on its own.
tasks.previous_blocker: The request was spoken, and the book was updated by retyping after the guest had left the desk.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system already holds room status, so a checked record can be stored without a second typing.
tasks.still_hard: A guest can change dates, ask for a room type that is not free, or arrive without the name on the request.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk confirms the stay with the guest. A stored row is not that confirmation.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to retyping a reservation the clerk already confirmed. Hearing the guest and confirming stay at the desk.

reach.task: Pass a stay request to the desk
reach.learn: Store a reservation only after the desk clerk has confirmed it

evidence.claim: A reservation record can be filled from dates, names, and a room type the clerk has already confirmed, then stored.
Confirming a stay binds the property to the guest, so the clerk confirms it and no unattended booking is made.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest asks and ends when the accepted reservation is stored. Rates, deposits, and group contracts stay outside it.

The stored fields are arrival date, departure date, guest name, room type, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the acceptance. If a field is missing, the row stays blank and the clerk types it. Nothing is taken from a call recording.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps disagree: only the write of an already confirmed reservation is automatic. The confirm itself stays with the clerk.
Upkeep is keeping room-type codes aligned with the property system.
unknowns: Whether the booking channel already creates a held reservation, so the write is smaller than assumed.
Which room types the property system treats as free for a same-day request.
research_questions: Which reservation fields does the property system already require before a stay can be stored?
Does any channel create a held reservation before the clerk confirms it?

already_counted.description: Reading the filled reservation is about half of the review, and that time stays in the step

incremental.description: Keep room-type codes aligned with the property system

approvals.approved_version: reservation the hotel desk clerk confirmed after the guest asked

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the channel already holds the reservation, the write disappears and the low end is only the small check of fields that still need a clerk. Hearing the guest and the spoken confirm stay either way. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Greet guests, register them, and assign rooms.

steps.what: Greet guests of hotels or motels.
Register guests and check the document they show.
Assign rooms the clerk chose for those guests.
Record the rooms after the clerk assigns them.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk greets the guest, checks the document, and assigns the room. {OPS_SYSTEM} records that assignment and does not choose the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assignment was written again after the guest had already been given the room.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system can store a room the clerk has just assigned.
tasks.still_hard: The guest may need a different room, a late arrival may have no document, and two clerks may be looking at the same room.
tasks.human_edge: Greeting the guest and choosing the room stay with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: The greeting and the room choice stay. Only the second typing of an assignment the clerk already made is shorter.

reach.task: Prepare the room the desk named
reach.learn: Use the room only after the desk clerk has assigned it

evidence.claim: A room assignment can be stored from the room number the clerk has already chosen.
Checking an identity document and assigning a room are decisions about a person, so they stay with the clerk.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest reaches the desk and ends when the assigned room is stored. Key handover and payment stay outside it.

The stored fields are guest name, document type, room number, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the room number. A missing document stops the write. No copy of the document is kept beyond what the property already requires.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the greeting and the assignment, and only the later record is a write.
Upkeep is keeping the list of room numbers that the desk may assign.
unknowns: Whether housekeepers already see the assignment inside the property system.
Which identity fields the property is allowed to store under national rules.
research_questions: Does the property system already show the assigned room to housekeeping?
Which identity fields must the desk see, and which must it not store?

already_counted.description: Checking the document is part of registering and stays in that step

incremental.description: Keep the list of rooms the desk may assign

approvals.approved_version: rooms the hotel desk clerk assigned after registering the guest

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the guest's channel already named a room, the clerk still greets and may still change it, so the low end keeps almost all of the desk time. The record is the only part that can shrink. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Verify credit and establish how the guest pays.

steps.what: Verify customers credit for the accommodation.
Establish how the customer will pay.
Run the card hold the terminal already performs.
Record the payment method the clerk established.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk verifies the guest and establishes the payment method. The card terminal's existing hold is left as it is. {OPS_SYSTEM} stores only the method the clerk established. No creditworthiness score is produced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The method was retyped after the clerk had already agreed it with the guest, and a separate note was easy to lose.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system can store a payment method the clerk has named, beside the hold the terminal already takes.
tasks.still_hard: A card can fail, a guest can pay by invoice, and the clerk still has to decide whether the stay goes ahead.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk decides whether the guest may stay and how the stay will be paid. A stored method is not that decision.
tasks.altitude: The credit check and the choice of payment stay with the clerk. Only the retype of the method they already chose is shorter.

reach.task: Match a stay to the method the desk stored
reach.learn: Read the method only after the desk clerk has established it

evidence.claim: A payment method the clerk has named can be stored as a short code on the stay.
A decision about a guest's credit has a legal effect, so it stays with the clerk and is not produced by a score.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest is at the desk and ends when the method the clerk established is stored. Granting credit, raising a limit, and refusing a stay stay outside it.

The stored fields are stay id, method code, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the method. The terminal hold is a separate existing step and is not an input to the stored method. No new credit check is sent anywhere.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. The terminal hold is work the machine already does and is not counted as clerk time saved.
Upkeep is keeping the short list of payment-method codes.
unknowns: Whether the property system already stores the method the terminal used.
Which invoice guests are allowed to leave without a card, under the property's own rule.
research_questions: Does the terminal already write the method onto the stay?
Who at the property may accept an invoice instead of a card?

already_counted.description: Verifying customers credit stays inside that step and is not new work

approvals.approved_version: payment method the hotel desk clerk established for this stay

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the terminal already writes the method onto the stay, the record step goes and the low end is only the clerk's check and the choice of how to pay, which do not shrink. The card hold is excluded either way. 26 percent is work the system already does and is not saved human labour. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Post extra charges the clerk accepted to ledgers.

steps.what: Post room charges the ledger already holds.
Hear liquor or telephone charges not yet posted.
Check those charges against the guest ledgers.
Accept only the charges the clerk heard.
Post accepted charges to ledgers using computers.

tasks.design: Room charges that {OPS_SYSTEM} already posts stay as they are. The hotel desk clerk hears an extra liquor or telephone charge, checks it against the ledger, and accepts it. {OPS_SYSTEM} posts only that accepted extra.
tasks.previous_blocker: Extras were written onto the ledger by hand after the guest had already agreed them.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system can post an amount and a code the clerk has accepted, next to the room charge it already posts.
tasks.still_hard: A guest may dispute a charge, and a minibar or a call may not match what the clerk heard.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk accepts the extra charge. The system does not decide that a guest owes it.
tasks.altitude: Room charges the system already posts are untouched. The clerk still hears and accepts extras. Only the retype of an accepted extra is shorter.

reach.learn: Treat an extra as posted only after the desk clerk accepted it

evidence.claim: An extra charge can be posted from an amount and a code the clerk has accepted.
Posting a charge the guest has not accepted changes what they owe, so the clerk accepts it first.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the clerk hears an extra and ends when that extra is posted. Room charges the system already posts, and any later dispute, stay outside it.
The posted fields are stay id, charge code, amount, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the amount. A charge with no acceptance is not posted.
The prior treats the whole task as automate. The steps disagree: the room-charge post is existing system work and is not saved clerk labour. Only an extra the clerk accepted is a new write.
Upkeep is keeping the charge codes for liquor and telephone calls.
unknowns: Whether every outlet already posts its own charges into the same ledger.
What the property does with a charge the guest refuses at the desk.
research_questions: Which charge codes does the property system already post without the clerk?
Who may reverse a posted extra after the guest has left?

already_counted.description: Checking heard charges against the ledger stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep liquor and telephone charge codes current

approvals.approved_version: extra charges the hotel desk clerk accepted after hearing them

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If every outlet already posts its own charges, the extra write disappears and the low end falls to the hearing and the acceptance, which stay. The existing room-charge post is excluded in both cases. 30 percent is work the system already does and is not saved human labour. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Greeting guests, confirming a stay, and deciding how the guest will pay stay at the desk. Retyping a reservation, a room assignment, a payment method, or an extra charge the clerk has already accepted takes less of the shift.
reach: Housekeeping sees a room only after the desk clerk has assigned it
A ledger extra exists only after the desk clerk has accepted that charge
skills_to_grow: Confirming a reservation with the guest before it is stored
Establishing the payment method without a credit score
Accepting an extra charge before it is posted
role.ambitious_version: Every stored reservation, room assignment, and extra charge is the version the desk clerk accepted while the guest was there.

job.title: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
